article.title: Present Perfect vs. Past Simple
article.description: Present Perfect (have/has + past participle) is used for actions with a connection to now, or when the exact time isn't stated: 'I have visited Paris.' Past Simple is used for finished actions at a specific, stated past time: 'I visited Paris in 2019.' Common mistake: using Present Perfect with a specific past time marker, e.g. 'I have visited Paris in 2019' is incorrect — should be Past Simple.

generated.caption:
Ever confused when to use "I have visited" vs. "I visited"? 🤔

Present Perfect (have + participle) connects actions to now, or when time isn't stated: "I have visited Paris." Past Simple is for finished actions at a *specific* past time: "I visited Paris in 2019." Crucially, don't use Present Perfect with specific past times!

slides.headlineRest: vs. Past Simple: The Key Difference
slides.body: The Present Perfect (have/has + past participle) connects past actions to the present, or is used when the exact time isn't mentioned. For example, 'I have visited Paris.' In contrast, the Past Simple describes actions completed at a specific, stated time in the past, like 'I visited Paris in 2019.' A common mistake is using the Present Perfect with a specific past time marker. For instance, 'I have visited Paris in 2019' is incorrect; the Past Simple 'I visited Paris in 2019' is the right choice when a precise time is given.
